legislationRegister.title: Directive 2014/53/EU on the harmonisation of the laws of the Member States relating to the making available on the market of radio equipment (Radio Equipment Directive)
legislationRegister.applicabilityPrinciple: Applies to 'radio equipment': any product that intentionally transmits and/or receives radio waves for radiocommunication or radiodetermination, or any product that must be fitted with an accessory such as an antenna to do so (definition reproduced in PT DL 57/2017 Art 3(h), EVD-MC11-317). A device with no intentional radio function is not radio equipment even if it contains a microcontroller. Where the RED applies it carries the safety/health, EMC and efficient-spectrum essential requirements for that equipment (EVD-MC11-304), so the EMC Directive does not additionally apply to it.

keyDeadlines.description: RED applicable as of 13 June 2016; transitional period ended 12 June 2017 (Article 48).

Repeal of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/30 (Articles 3(3)(d), (e), (f)) by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/339 takes effect, the same date the CRA main obligations begin; from then the CRA carries the radio-cybersecurity requirements.

legislationRegister.title: Directive 2014/30/EU on the harmonisation of the laws of the Member States relating to electromagnetic compatibility (EMC Directive)
legislationRegister.applicabilityPrinciple: Applies to apparatus and fixed installations placed on the market and/or taken into service: equipment must not generate electromagnetic disturbance that prevents radio and telecommunication or other equipment from working as intended, and must have adequate immunity (EVD-MC11-307). It does not apply to equipment covered by the RED, which carries its own EMC essential requirement; the national transposition states the exclusion expressly (PT DL 57/2017 Art 2(2): radio equipment covered by that decree-law is not subject to the EMC transposition Decreto-Lei n.º 31/2017 except for the safety provision of Article 4(1)(a), EVD-MC11-317).

keyDeadlines.description: EMC Directive 2014/30/EU applies and repeals Directive 2004/108/EC as from 20 April 2016.

legislationRegister.title: Directive 2014/35/EU on the harmonisation of the laws of the Member States relating to the making available on the market of electrical equipment designed for use within certain voltage limits (Low Voltage Directive)
legislationRegister.applicabilityPrinciple: Applies to electrical equipment operating with an input or output voltage between 50 and 1000 V AC or between 75 and 1500 V DC (EVD-MC11-306). Equipment whose supply and internal circuits stay below both thresholds is outside the LVD. The directive does not require notified-body assessment; the manufacturer alone determines compliance.

legislationRegister.title: Directive 2011/65/EU on the restriction of the use of certain hazardous substances in electrical and electronic equipment (RoHS recast)
legislationRegister.applicabilityPrinciple: Applies to electrical and electronic equipment, including cables and spare parts, with an annex list of categories plus an open catch-all category relevant from July 2019 and a short exclusion list that does not cover marine navigation or instrument electronics (EVD-MC11-313). It is a CE-marking act: the manufacturer must design and produce to the substance restrictions and hold technical documentation; importers must check and distributors must verify.

keyDeadlines.description: Open catch-all EEE category applies from July 2019 (the retrieved summary renders the month, not the exact day; day shown for machine ordering and flagged for confirmation).

legislationRegister.title: Directive 2012/19/EU on waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE recast), as amended by Directive (EU) 2024/884
legislationRegister.applicabilityPrinciple: Applies to EEE placed on the EU market and imposes producer responsibility: registration of producers/importers in a national register, free take-back, collection and treatment targets, and financing of collection, treatment, recovery and disposal (EVD-MC11-314). Exclusions listed in the retrieved summary are military/space material, filament bulbs, active implantable medical devices and means of transport; a navigation or instrument accessory is not a means of transport. WEEE does not impose CE marking.

keyDeadlines.description: Minimum annual WEEE collection rate rises to 65 % 'from 2019' per the retrieved summary (exact date not rendered).

legislationRegister.title: Regulation (EU) 2023/988 on general product safety (General Product Safety Regulation)
legislationRegister.applicabilityPrinciple: Applies to products made available on the EU market that are not covered by other specific EU product-safety legislation, and to the risks and aspects not already covered by such legislation (EVD-MC11-308). It therefore sits alongside the RED/EMC/RoHS requirements rather than replacing them: general safety, foreseeable misuse, installation, thermal and mechanical hazards, warnings and traceability are GPSR matters. It requires a responsible economic operator in the EU, a risk analysis, technical documentation, traceability, a complaints register, incident reporting and recall capability. GPSR does not require CE marking.

keyDeadlines.description: GPSR applies from 13 December 2024 — the application date was NOT rendered on the retrieved EUR-Lex summary and is carried forward from MC-02 C-05; flagged for qualified confirmation.

legislationRegister.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 on horizontal cybersecurity requirements for products with digital elements and amending Regulations (EU) No 168/2013 and (EU) 2019/1020 and Directive (EU) 2020/1828 (Cyber Resilience Act)
legislationRegister.applicabilityPrinciple: Applies to products with digital elements placed on the EU market, wherever the manufacturer is based, whose intended or reasonably foreseeable use includes a direct or indirect logical or physical data connection to a device or network; the scope expressly covers both hardware and software products (EVD-MC11-302). 'Important' and 'critical' products face stricter conformity assessment, with technical descriptions in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2392 (EVD-MC11-302). Marine equipment within the scope of Directive 2014/90/EU is excluded (EVD-MC11-302) — an exclusion that does NOT cover recreational-craft electronics outside MED scope. CRA is a CE-marking act.

keyDeadlines.description: CRA entered into force on 10 December 2024.

Reporting obligations apply from 11 September 2026 (Article 71(2)); ENISA CRA Single Reporting Platform operational the same day; early warning within 24 h, full notification within 72 h, final report within 14 days of a corrective measure (vulnerabilities) or one month after the 72-hour notification (severe incidents).

CRA main obligations apply from 11 December 2027, including cybersecurity requirements, vulnerability handling during the support period, technical documentation, declaration of conformity and CE marking.

legislationRegister.title: Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 concerning batteries and waste batteries, amending Directive 2008/98/EC and Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 and repealing Directive 2006/66/EC
legislationRegister.applicabilityPrinciple: Applies to all batteries placed on the EU market regardless of origin, composition or whether sold separately or incorporated into a product, covering portable, LMT, EV, industrial and SLI batteries (EVD-MC11-309). Any battery inside a MAREA product is a portable battery and brings the configuration into scope: substance restrictions, safety and durability criteria, labelling from 2026, QR code from 2027, producer collection/recycling obligations, and the requirement that portable batteries incorporated into appliances be removable and replaceable by the end user by 2027 (EVD-MC11-310).

legislationRegister.title: Directive 2014/90/EU on marine equipment and repealing Council Directive 96/98/EC (Marine Equipment Directive)
legislationRegister.applicabilityPrinciple: Applies to equipment on ships flying an EU flag that are subject to the international conventions, requires assessment by an independent third party (notified body) and the 'wheel mark', and is complemented by annual implementing acts listing the equipment and the applicable testing standards (EVD-MC11-311). A recreational craft is not such a ship. The directive is not applied automatically to recreational-craft electronics in this milestone; that determination is reasoned and flagged for legal review.

legislationRegister.title: Directive 2013/53/EU on recreational craft and personal watercraft and repealing Directive 94/25/EC (Recreational Craft Directive)
legislationRegister.applicabilityPrinciple: Applies to watercraft, designated components and propulsion engines placed on the EU market, with design categories A-D, CE marking on the craft builder's plate and a set of essential requirements (identification number, builder's plate, reboarding, visibility, manual, structure/stability/buoyancy, emergency stopping device) (EVD-MC11-315).
